correctness.rationale: The Fraïssé extension property identifies one-types with ideal/filter pairs L<U, with no quotient by automorphisms of named parameters. For maximal parameter x, D={q<x} ideal of Q=P\{x}, F=Q\D, an exact trichotomy of x<new, new<x and incomparable yields t(P)-t(Q)=J(D)+J(F)+E_Q(D). Lower bounds J(R)>=|R|+1 give chain minimum; at most 2t(Q)+1 gives antichain maximum. For Q chain and D prefix length k, excess g(P)=(k+1)(m-k), minimized for nonchain at k=0,m−1. For Q nonchain induction and equality of ideal-count contributions imply only doubled-level or one isolated-point families. Independent new subset-based type enumerator checked all naturally ordered transitive relations n2..5 (2,7,40,357), confirming both extrema, runner-up value and exact equality shapes. Infinite induction, not finite scan, establishes all n.

value.rationale: For a natural homogeneous structure, the count of one-point types over a named finite parameter configuration is a standard orbit-growth invariant. The exact strict gap above chains and classification of all minimizers is a meaningful structural extremal theorem rather than a routine count for a single chosen finite poset; it identifies the first two tiers of the full n-parameter type spectrum.

final_claim: For the countable universal homogeneous strict partial order, the nonalgebraic complete one-type count t(P) over n>=2 individually named finite parameters lies between binom(n+2,2) and 2^(n+1)-1, with equality only for a chain/antichain respectively. For nonchains, t(P)>=binom(n+2,2)+n-1, with equality precisely for C_(n-1) disjoint union C1 or C_a ordinal-sum A2 ordinal-sum C_b where a+b=n-2.
limitations: n>=2 finite strict parameter posets, pointwise named elements; counts nonalgebraic complete 1-types.
Does not prove second maximum, monotonicity under adding one comparison, or a polynomial-time general counting algorithm.
